title: 22. Autoscaling & Consolidation (KEDA & Karpenter)
summary: Master intelligent event-driven workload autoscaling with KEDA (Kubernetes Event-driven Autoscaling) and rapid node provisioning and consolidation with Karpenter.
prerequisites: Horizontal Pod Autoscaler (HPA) and Metrics Server
Cloud Provider Auto Scaling Groups / VM Scale Sets
learningObjectives: Deploy KEDA ScaledObject and TriggerAuthentication resources for queue-length autoscaling down to zero
Configure Karpenter NodePool and EC2NodeClass resources for sub-minute node provisioning
Implement Karpenter consolidation policies to eliminate underutilized cloud compute instances
Protect mission-critical production services with fine-tuned PodDisruptionBudgets (PDB)

curriculumModules.title: KEDA: Event-Driven Autoscaling Beyond CPU/Memory
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Standard HPA is reactive and bounded to CPU/memory metrics. KEDA provides 60+ external scalers (Kafka, Redis, RabbitMQ, SQS, Prometheus) and supports scale-to-zero when queues are idle.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Microservice workers scaling from 0 to 100 pods based on Kafka consumer group lag or SQS queue depth.

curriculumModules.title: Karpenter: High-Velocity Node Autoscaling & Consolidation
curriculumModules.conceptSummary: Karpenter bypasses slow Cloud Auto Scaling Groups by directly evaluating unschedulable pod resource requirements and launching optimal EC2/Compute instances in < 45 seconds.
curriculumModules.productionArchitecturePattern: Dynamic Karpenter NodePool with consolidationPolicy: WhenUnderutilized and spot instance interruption handling.

labs.title: KEDA Event-Driven Queue Autoscaling Configuration
labs.scenario: Your asynchronous image processing service experiences unpredictable bursts. Configure a KEDA ScaledObject that scales the worker Deployment from 1 to 20 replicas based on queue lag.
labs.productionContext: KEDA automatically creates and manages the underlying Kubernetes HPA, feeding it external custom metrics from message brokers.
objectives: Deploy the order-worker Deployment with 1 initial replica
Deploy a KEDA ScaledObject named worker-scaler targeting order-worker
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: order-worker
  namespace: production
spec:
  replicas: 1
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: order-worker
  template:
    metadata:
      labels:
        app: order-worker
    spec:
      containers:
        - name: worker
          image: busybox:1.36
          command: ["sh", "-c", "while true; do sleep 10; done"]
---
apiVersion: keda.sh/v1alpha1
kind: ScaledObject
metadata:
  name: worker-scaler
  namespace: production
spec:
  scaleTargetRef:
    name: order-worker
  minReplicaCount: 1
  maxReplicaCount: 20
  pollingInterval: 15
  cooldownPeriod: 60

steps.title: Review KEDA ScaledObject Manifest
steps.instruction: Open the Manifest Editor and review the order-worker Deployment and worker-scaler ScaledObject.

steps.title: Deploy Workload and ScaledObject
steps.instruction: Apply the manifest to the production namespace.

validationRules.description: Deployment order-worker exists in production namespace
validationRules.name: order-worker
validationRules.remediation: Apply the starter manifest to create the order-worker Deployment.

labs.title: Karpenter NodePool Consolidation & PodDisruptionBudgets
labs.scenario: To optimize cloud costs, configure a Karpenter NodePool with consolidationPolicy WhenUnderutilized, protected by a PodDisruptionBudget ensuring 80% minimum availability.
labs.productionContext: Karpenter consolidation dynamically replaces multiple underutilized nodes with fewer, cheaper instances, cutting cloud bills by up to 50%.
objectives: Deploy a Karpenter NodePool named general-compute with consolidation enabled
Deploy a PodDisruptionBudget named payment-pdb requiring minAvailable: 80%
Verify node scheduling and consolidation policies
labs.starterManifest:
apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1
kind: NodePool
metadata:
  name: general-compute
spec:
  disruption:
    consolidationPolicy: WhenUnderutilized
    consolidateAfter: 30s
  template:
    spec:
      nodeClassRef:
        name: default
---
apiVersion: policy/v1
kind: PodDisruptionBudget
metadata:
  name: payment-pdb
  namespace: production
spec:
  minAvailable: "80%"
  selector:
    matchLabels:
      app: payment-api

steps.title: Inspect Karpenter and PDB Manifests
steps.instruction: Review the NodePool and PodDisruptionBudget definitions in the Manifest Editor.

steps.title: Apply NodePool and PDB Resources
steps.instruction: Deploy the resources to establish consolidation and disruption protection.

validationRules.description: NodePool general-compute exists with consolidationPolicy WhenUnderutilized
validationRules.name: general-compute
validationRules.remediation: Apply the NodePool manifest with spec.disruption.consolidationPolicy: WhenUnderutilized.

validationRules.description: PodDisruptionBudget payment-pdb exists in production with minAvailable 80%
validationRules.name: payment-pdb
validationRules.remediation: Deploy PodDisruptionBudget payment-pdb in production with minAvailable: '80%'.

labs.troubleshootingGuide: Ensure minAvailable in the PDB is passed as a string with percentage '80%'.

assessmentQuestions.question: What is the primary capability KEDA introduces over standard Kubernetes Horizontal Pod Autoscaler?
options: It can scale workloads based on external event sources (queues, streams) and scale down to zero replicas
It replaces the kubelet on worker nodes
It only works with Java applications
assessmentQuestions.explanation: KEDA provides event-driven scalers for 60+ external systems and enables scale-to-zero when event queues are empty.

assessmentQuestions.question: How does Karpenter consolidation optimize cluster compute costs?
options: By deleting idle pods every 5 minutes
By identifying underutilized nodes, evicting workloads according to PDBs, and terminating or downsizing EC2 instances
By enforcing mandatory spot instances on control-plane nodes
assessmentQuestions.explanation: Karpenter consolidation continuously monitors cluster utilization and consolidates workloads onto fewer, cheaper nodes.
